<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="EncycloPetey" />{{rh|BK. xiii.]|FAREWELL SPEECHES OF ULYSSES.|169}}</noinclude>eyes towards the sun, as though to hasten his setting, for he was longing to be on his way. As one who has been all day ploughing a fallow field with a couple of oxen keeps thinking about his supper and is glad when night comes that he may go and get it, for it is all his legs can do to carry him, even so did Ulysses rejoice when the sun went down, and he at once said to the Phæacians, addressing himself more particularly to King Alcinous:—

{{pline|38|l}}"Sir, and all of you, farewell. Make your drink-offerings and send me on my way rejoicing, for you have fulfilled my heart's desire by giving me an escort, and making me presents, which heaven grant that I may turn to good account; may I find my admirable wife living in peace among friends,<ref>I suppose Teiresias' prophecy of bk. xi. 114—120 had made no impression on Ulysses. More probably the prophecy was an afterthought, intercalated, as I have already said, by the authoress when she changed her scheme.</ref> and may you whom I leave behind me give satisfaction to your wives and children<ref>A male writer would have made Ulysses say, not "may you give satisfaction to your wives," but "may your wives give satisfaction to you."</ref>; may heaven vouchsafe you every good grace, and may no evil thing come among your people."

{{pline|47|l}}Thus did he speak. His hearers all of them approved his saying and agreed that he should have his escort inasmuch as he had spoken reasonably. Alcinous therefore said to his servant, "Pontonous, mix some wine and hand it round to everybody, that we may offer a prayer to father Jove, and speed our guest upon his way."

{{pline|53|l}}Pontonous mixed the wine and handed it to every one in turn; the others each from his own seat made a drink-offering to the blessed gods that live in heaven, but Ulysses rose and placed the double cup in the hands of queen Arēte.

{{pline|59|l}}"Farewell, queen," said he, "henceforward and for ever, till age and death, the common lot of mankind, lay their hands upon you. I now take my leave; be happy in this house with your children, your people, and with king Alcinous."
